\chapter{Tickets, Seats and Trouble}
\label{ch:ta-tickets-seats-and-trouble}
\hlchaptermodality{289}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can buy a ticket with … oru cīṭṭu koṭuṅkaḷ, ask for a seat (irukkai) and when a train leaves, and report a problem: a bag that is missing (kāṇavillai), a passport that is lost, a bus I missed.}

Complete the last lesson of chapter 289: buy a ticket, ask for a seat and a time, and report something lost or missed.
\end{chapteropening}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ta{இருக்கை} (irukkai)}{இருக்கை (irukkai)}]{\ta{இருக்கை} (irukkai) — a seat}

\label{lesson:TA-C289-irukkai}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the words for a bus, a train and a passenger. (\emph{pēruntu}, \emph{rayil}, \emph{payaṇi}.) Then \textquotedblleft{}to be, to stay\textquotedblright{}. (\emph{iru}.)
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ta{இருக்கை}}
\textbf{\ta{இருக்கை}} — \emph{irukkai} — \textquotedblleft{}a seat\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\textbf{\ta{இது} \ta{உங்கள்} \ta{இருக்கையா}?}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{itu uṅkaḷ irukkaiyā?} — \textquotedblleft{}Is this your seat?\textquotedblright{}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\textbf{\ta{பேருந்தில்} \ta{இருக்கை} \ta{இல்லை}.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{pēruntil irukkai illai.} — \textquotedblleft{}There is no seat on the bus.\textquotedblright{}
\end{quote}

You can hear \textbf{\ta{இரு}} at its front: a seat is a place to be. On a bus, in a train, in a cinema or a hall, \textbf{\ta{இருக்கை}} is the word for the place you sit.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ta{இருக்கை}} (\emph{irukkai}) is native Dravidian. DEDR 480 lists Tamil \emph{irukkai}, \textquotedblleft{}sitting, seat, residence\textquotedblright{}, under \emph{iru}, which it glosses \textquotedblleft{}to exist, remain, sit down\textquotedblright{}. So the verb you know as \textquotedblleft{}to be, to stay\textquotedblright{} also meant \textquotedblleft{}to sit\textquotedblright{}, and the seat is named from it.
\end{cousinweb}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{irukkai}, slowly, then at speed
  \item \textquotedblleft{}Is this your seat?\textquotedblright{} — \emph{itu uṅkaḷ irukkaiyā?}
  \item \textquotedblleft{}There is no seat on the bus\textquotedblright{} — \emph{pēruntil irukkai illai}
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \textbf{\ta{இருக்கை}} mean? (\textbf{A seat.}) \textquotedblleft{}Is this your seat?\textquotedblright{} (\textbf{\ta{இது} \ta{உங்கள்} \ta{இருக்கையா}?}) Which verb can you hear inside it? (\textbf{\ta{இரு}}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ta{ஒரு} \ta{சீட்டு} \ta{கொடுங்கள்} (oru cīṭṭu koṭuṅkaḷ)}{ஒரு சீட்டு கொடுங்கள் (oru cīṭṭu koṭuṅkaḷ)}]{\ta{ஒரு} \ta{சீட்டு} \ta{கொடுங்கள்} (oru cīṭṭu koṭuṅkaḷ) — tickets and times}

\label{lesson:TA-C289-cittu-kotunkal}



\begin{quote}
Say \textquotedblleft{}a ticket\textquotedblright{} (\emph{cīṭṭu}) and \textquotedblleft{}a seat\textquotedblright{} (\emph{irukkai}). Then say \textquotedblleft{}dampness\textquotedblright{}. (\emph{īram}.)
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: buying a ticket}
\begin{quote}
\textbf{\ta{மதுரைக்கு} \ta{இரண்டு} \ta{சீட்டு} \ta{கொடுங்கள்}.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{maturaikku iraṇṭu cīṭṭu koṭuṅkaḷ.} — \textquotedblleft{}Two tickets to Madurai, please.\textquotedblright{}
\end{quote}

The place you are going takes \textbf{-\ta{க்கு}}: \textbf{\ta{மதுரைக்கு}}, \textquotedblleft{}to Madurai\textquotedblright{}, a city in the south of Tamil Nadu. \textbf{\ta{கொடுங்கள்}} is \textbf{\ta{கொடு}} with the polite \textbf{-\ta{உங்கள்}}: \textquotedblleft{}give (me)\textquotedblright{}. After a number Tamil often leaves the noun as it is: \textbf{\ta{இரண்டு} \ta{சீட்டு}}. For seats side by side: \textbf{\ta{இரண்டு} \ta{இருக்கைகள்} \ta{சேர்ந்து} \ta{வேண்டும்}} (\emph{iraṇṭu irukkaikaḷ cērntu vēṇṭum}, \textquotedblleft{}I need two seats together\textquotedblright{}); \textbf{\ta{சேர்ந்து}} is \textquotedblleft{}having joined\textquotedblright{}, from \textbf{\ta{சேர்}}.

\subsection*{You'll want to know: when does it leave?}
\begin{quote}
\textbf{\ta{மதுரைக்கு} \ta{ரயில்} \ta{எத்தனை} \ta{மணிக்குப்} \ta{புறப்படும்}?}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{maturaikku rayil ettaṉai maṇikkup puṟappaṭum?} — \textquotedblleft{}What time does the train to Madurai leave?\textquotedblright{}
\end{quote}

\textbf{\ta{எத்தனை} \ta{மணிக்கு}}, \textquotedblleft{}at what hour\textquotedblright{}. \textbf{\ta{புறப்படும்}} is the \textquotedblleft{}it\textquotedblright{} future of \textbf{\ta{புறப்படு}}, \textquotedblleft{}to set out\textquotedblright{}: \textquotedblleft{}it will set out\textquotedblright{}. Tamil uses it for a timetable, where English says \textquotedblleft{}leaves\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\textbf{\ta{ரயில்} \ta{ஆறு} \ta{மணிக்குப்} \ta{புறப்படும்}. \ta{எட்டு} \ta{மணிக்கு} \ta{மதுரைக்குப்} \ta{போய்ச்} \ta{சேரும்}.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{rayil āṟu maṇikkup puṟappaṭum. eṭṭu maṇikku maturaikkup pōyc cērum.} — \textquotedblleft{}The train leaves at six. It gets to Madurai at eight.\textquotedblright{}
\end{quote}

\textbf{\ta{போய்ச்} \ta{சேரும்}}: \textquotedblleft{}having gone, it will reach\textquotedblright{}, with \textbf{\ta{சேர்}}, \textquotedblleft{}to reach\textquotedblright{}.

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \textquotedblleft{}Two tickets to Madurai, please\textquotedblright{} — \emph{maturaikku iraṇṭu cīṭṭu koṭuṅkaḷ}
  \item \textquotedblleft{}I need two seats together\textquotedblright{} — \emph{iraṇṭu irukkaikaḷ cērntu vēṇṭum}
  \item \textquotedblleft{}What time does the train to Madurai leave?\textquotedblright{} — \emph{maturaikku rayil ettaṉai maṇikkup puṟappaṭum?}
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
\textquotedblleft{}Two tickets, please\textquotedblright{}? (\textbf{\ta{இரண்டு} \ta{சீட்டு} \ta{கொடுங்கள்}}.) \textquotedblleft{}To Madurai\textquotedblright{}? (\textbf{\ta{மதுரைக்கு}}.) \textquotedblleft{}What time does it leave?\textquotedblright{} (\textbf{\ta{எத்தனை} \ta{மணிக்குப்} \ta{புறப்படும்}?}) \textquotedblleft{}It gets there at eight\textquotedblright{}? (\textbf{\ta{எட்டு} \ta{மணிக்குப்} \ta{போய்ச்} \ta{சேரும்}}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ta{காணவில்லை} (kāṇavillai)}{காணவில்லை (kāṇavillai)}]{\ta{காணவில்லை} (kāṇavillai) — missing, lost, missed}

\label{lesson:TA-C289-kanavillai}



\begin{quote}
Say \textquotedblleft{}One ticket, please.\textquotedblright{} (\emph{oru cīṭṭu koṭuṅkaḷ}.) Then the words for \textquotedblleft{}to miss\textquotedblright{} and \textquotedblleft{}a complaint\textquotedblright{}. (\emph{tavaṟaviṭu}, \emph{pukār}.) Then \textquotedblleft{}it has got late\textquotedblright{}. (\emph{nēramākiviṭṭatu}.)
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: missing and lost}
\begin{quote}
\textbf{\ta{என்} \ta{பையைக்} \ta{காணவில்லை}.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{eṉ paiyaik kāṇavillai.} — \textquotedblleft{}My bag is missing.\textquotedblright{}
\end{quote}

\textbf{\ta{காணவில்லை}} is \textquotedblleft{}not seen\textquotedblright{}: \textbf{\ta{காண்}}, \textquotedblleft{}to see\textquotedblright{}, the old verb inside \textbf{\ta{கனவு} \ta{காண்}}, with the \textbf{-\ta{வில்லை}} of \textbf{\ta{புரியவில்லை}}. The missing thing takes \textbf{-\ta{ஐ}}, as a thing you look for: \textbf{\ta{பையை}}. A notice about someone or something lost is headed with this one word.

\begin{quote}
\textbf{\ta{என்} \ta{கடவுச்சீட்டு} \ta{தொலைந்துவிட்டது}.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{eṉ kaṭavuccīṭṭu tolaintuviṭṭatu.} — \textquotedblleft{}My passport has got lost.\textquotedblright{}
\end{quote}

\textbf{\ta{தொலை}} (\emph{tolai}, \textquotedblleft{}to get lost\textquotedblright{}). \textbf{\ta{தொலைந்துவிட்டது}} is its \textbf{-\ta{உ}} form with \textbf{\ta{விட்டது}}, \textquotedblleft{}it has gone and …\textquotedblright{}, the same \textbf{\ta{விட்டது}} as in \textbf{\ta{நேரமாகிவிட்டது}}: the thing is gone, and that is that.

\subsection*{You'll want to know: what you missed, and the complaint}
\begin{quote}
\textbf{\ta{நான்} \ta{பேருந்தைத்} \ta{தவறவிட்டேன்}.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{nāṉ pēruntait tavaṟaviṭṭēṉ.} — \textquotedblleft{}I missed the bus.\textquotedblright{}
\end{quote}

\textbf{\ta{தவறவிடு}} in the plain past: \textbf{\ta{தவறவிட்டேன்}}. The bus takes \textbf{-\ta{ஐ}}, and the first letter after it doubles in writing: \textbf{\ta{பேருந்தைத்} \ta{தவறவிட்டேன்}}.

\begin{quote}
\textbf{\ta{நான்} \ta{புகார்} \ta{கொடுக்க} \ta{வேண்டும்}. \ta{காவல்} \ta{நிலையம்} \ta{எங்கே} \ta{இருக்கிறது}?}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{nāṉ pukār koṭukka vēṇṭum. kāval nilaiyam eṅkē irukkiṟatu?} — \textquotedblleft{}I need to make a complaint. Where is the police station?\textquotedblright{}
\end{quote}

Tamil \textquotedblleft{}gives\textquotedblright{} a complaint: \textbf{\ta{புகார்} \ta{கொடு}}.

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \textquotedblleft{}My bag is missing\textquotedblright{} — \emph{eṉ paiyaik kāṇavillai}
  \item \textquotedblleft{}My passport has got lost\textquotedblright{} — \emph{eṉ kaṭavuccīṭṭu tolaintuviṭṭatu}
  \item \textquotedblleft{}I missed the bus\textquotedblright{} — \emph{nāṉ pēruntait tavaṟaviṭṭēṉ}
  \item \textquotedblleft{}I need to make a complaint. Where is the police station?\textquotedblright{} — \emph{nāṉ pukār koṭukka vēṇṭum. kāval nilaiyam eṅkē irukkiṟatu?}
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
\textquotedblleft{}My bag is missing\textquotedblright{}? (\textbf{\ta{என்} \ta{பையைக்} \ta{காணவில்லை}}.) \textquotedblleft{}It has got lost\textquotedblright{}? (\textbf{\ta{தொலைந்துவிட்டது}}.) \textquotedblleft{}I missed the bus\textquotedblright{}? (\textbf{\ta{பேருந்தைத்} \ta{தவறவிட்டேன்}}.) \textquotedblleft{}To make a complaint\textquotedblright{}? (\textbf{\ta{புகார்} \ta{கொடு}}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[(review)]{Review — at the station}

\label{lesson:TA-R289-at-the-station}



\begin{quote}
Say \textquotedblleft{}a seat\textquotedblright{} and \textquotedblleft{}a ticket\textquotedblright{}. Then read \textbf{\ta{ஈரம்}} aloud: which letter opens it? (\textbf{\ta{ஈ}}, \emph{ī}.)

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Write it:} \textbf{\ta{இருக்கை}} and \textbf{\ta{சீட்டு}}, once each
\end{itemize}
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item One ticket to Madurai, please. What time does the bus leave?
  \item Is this your seat? No, my seat is there.
  \item I missed the train, because I came late.
  \item My bag is missing. Where is the police station?
  \item one thing that went wrong on a journey of yours, and what you did
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
\textquotedblleft{}A seat\textquotedblright{}? (\textbf{\ta{இருக்கை}}.) \textquotedblleft{}What time does it leave?\textquotedblright{} (\textbf{\ta{எத்தனை} \ta{மணிக்குப்} \ta{புறப்படும்}?}) \textquotedblleft{}My bag is missing\textquotedblright{}? (\textbf{\ta{என்} \ta{பையைக்} \ta{காணவில்லை}}.) \textquotedblleft{}I missed the bus\textquotedblright{}? (\textbf{\ta{பேருந்தைத்} \ta{தவறவிட்டேன்}}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
